name: Shortest Statement Ever
description: You are given two non-negative integers $$$x$$$, $$$y$$$. Find two non-negative integers $$$p$$$ and $$$q$$$ such that $$$p\;\&\;q=0$$$, and $$$|x-p|+|y-q|$$$ is minimized. Here, $$$\&$$$ denotes the bitwise AND operation .
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The only line of each test case contains two non-negative integers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ ($$$0 \le x,y \lt 2^{30}$$$).
output_specification: For each test case, output two non-negative integers $$$p$$$ and $$$q$$$ you found. If there are multiple pairs of $$$p$$$ and $$$q$$$ satisfying the conditions, you may output any of them. It can be proven that under the constraints of the problem, any valid solution satisfies $$$\max(p,q) \lt 2^{31}$$$.
approach_summary: Define state dp[mask][i] capturing the subset of visited/chosen elements. Transition by iterating over valid unset bits in O(2^N × N) time.
